official_measurement_examples.name: July 2026 guidance suite
official_measurement_examples.fact: The National Infrastructure Planning Guidance Portal records July 2026 guidance as in force, so older advice must retain its status and update context.

official_measurement_examples.name: Acceptance is not consent
official_measurement_examples.fact: Acceptance of a DCO application is a procedural gateway and is not the Secretary of State's decision to grant development consent.

official_measurement_examples.name: Decision stage separation
official_measurement_examples.fact: The decision-making stage follows examination and remains distinct from application acceptance, pre-application consultation and later implementation.

official_measurement_examples.name: Linear project land rights
official_measurement_examples.fact: Linear-project guidance requires land-rights and affected-person evidence; route proximity alone does not establish acquired rights over a parcel.

official_measurement_examples.name: Section 53 distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A right-of-entry authorisation for surveys is not a DCO, compulsory acquisition power or permanent right to use the land.

official_measurement_examples.name: Compulsory acquisition distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: Seeking compulsory acquisition powers within a DCO requires separate statutory justification and procedure; application inclusion is not proof that land has been acquired.

official_measurement_examples.name: DCO change process
official_measurement_examples.fact: A granted DCO can later be changed through material or non-material procedures; historic order geometry must retain version and change status.

official_measurement_examples.name: Project status limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: NSIP project records must retain stage such as pre-application, accepted, examination, recommendation, decision or post-consent; a project listing is not parcel development prohibition by itself.

core_rules: application acceptance is not development consent
pre-application project record is not a granted DCO
DCO grant is not proof all land rights have been acquired
section 53 survey entry is not permanent land right
compulsory acquisition request is not completed acquisition
route corridor geometry is not cadastral ownership
DCO changes must retain order version and effective date
project-stage labels must not be collapsed
NSIP evidence does not determine unrelated parcel planning capacity
no parcel NSIP clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
historic advice must not override July 2026 guidance status without checking current portal
source_verification_note: Official MHCLG, Planning Inspectorate and legislation.gov.uk sources checked on 2026-07-26; July 2026 NSIP guidance and advice updates retained with application/consent/land-right stage separation; no parcel promotion.
